title: Food banks highlight mobile markets amid increased demand - NewsBreak
text:
By Sean Graney ,
4 hours ago
JACKSON, Mich. (WLNS) — Communities across Mid-Michigan are preparing for one of the most important days of giving in years as food insecurity reaches new highs. Local food banks say mobile markets are becoming a lifeline, delivering fresh food directly into neighborhoods that need it most.
At Jackson College, Student Life Coordinator Maddy Woods says Harriet’s Hub Food Pantry has served 551 total households this fall, including 102 first-time students.
(WLNS) “Our partnership that we have with South Michigan Food Bank ensures that we are spending extremely low amounts of money for large quantities of food because we pay a very small price per pound for all of our food,” Woods said. “So, we’re able to get those giant quantities and fully stock our pantry regularly for those students.”
Woods says the mission goes beyond just class work — it’s about making sure students can actually focus on school without worrying about having food on the table.
“It’s not just your academics that we want to see you succeed, we want to see you succeed overall in life,” Woods said. “So, if that means that putting food on your table is part of that concern, we want to try and alleviate that. The best that we can.”
(WLNS) Dawn Foods Head of Corporate Giving Cherie Good says one of the biggest hurdles they see with food insecurity is simply getting residents to the food.
“Because transportation often can be one of the largest barriers for people,” Good said. “While we have a lot of great local pantries who are doing distribution, the reality of the situation is that we have to meet people where they are.”
(WLNS) Good says it’s not just about donations but getting more business to buy in and help support the pantries doing the day-to-day work.
“We really do want to encourage other corporate organizations to join us and helping to support not only the Food Bank but their local food partners who are doing the hard work, day in day out,” Good said.
Good says Dawn Foods will be hosting an emergency food bags distribution event Thursday ahead of the day of giving in order to reach residents who can’t make it out on Friday.
